sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in Indonesia financials, led by FUJI, TIFA, and TRUS, as domestic outperformance (+0.68%) versus US (-0.18%) signals resilient local credit demand and digital-payment adoption. Rotate into BBLD and BSWD for value exposure, while avoiding COIN volatility. Maintain overweight on banks with strong NIMs and fintech lenders; expect continued momentum as IDX liquidity favors small-caps.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesia's downstream processing mandate (smelter build-out) structurally re-rates nickel and copper miners like INCO and AMMN, insulating them from raw ore export bans.
Coal remains a durable cash generator despite ESG pressure, as domestic demand (PLN) and Asian spot prices above marginal costs support COAL and PSAB's dividend capacity.
Consolidation in the junior mining space, evidenced by ALKA's and BRMS's outsized moves, signals a wave of M&A and resource upgrades that rewards early movers with re-rating potential.
sectors.ai: Buy selective exposure to nickel and coal names on the back of firming global commodity prices and Indonesia's downstream policy tailwinds; prioritize AMMN and INCO for volume growth, but take profits on ALKA's speculative spike. Maintain a watch bias on the aggregate, as US macro volatility could cap upside; add on any 3-5% pullback in liquid large caps.

Indonesia's EV/battery supply chain is the durable local alpha: VKTR's bus electrification and downstream nickel processing align with the government's 2030 EV roadmap, but domestic policy execution a

sectors.ai: Buy dips in US-listed solar/energy storage names (SEDG, ENPH, RUN) as the AI-driven power demand narrative and IRA tailwinds persist; Indonesia's VKTR upside is real but liquidity-thin, so size positions small and pair with US hedges. sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rupiah stability and easing inflation are restoring real household purchasing power, a durable tailwind for mass-market FMCG volumes into 2025.
Formal retail channel consolidation and premiumization are shifting share to listed players with strong distribution, rewarding scale and brand investment.
Export-oriented consumer names (food, agri, fisheries) benefit from structural global demand and favorable FX, decoupling from domestic consumption cycles.
sectors.ai: Indonesian consumer/FMCG is in a selective re-rating, not a broad upcycle: leadership is concentrated in small/mid caps (EL, AGAR, BOGA) with idiosyncratic catalysts, while large caps lag. Position for quality names with proven earnings delivery and export/commodity-linked upside; avoid chasing momentum without volume confirmation. Trim into strength on names up >10% in one session, as retail-driven spikes fade fast.

sectors.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
themes: Ethereum's ETF inflows and staking yield are a durable structural bid, pulling capital into L2 ecosystems (ARB, MNT) that monetize ETH's activity.
High-beta altcoins (HYPE, WLD) are now a proxy for global risk appetite, with retail leverage and AI narratives driving outsized moves independent of Indonesia's local regulatory lag.
Stablecoin and tokenization adoption in Southeast Asia, including Indonesia's pending crypto rules, will eventually funnel domestic liquidity into global majors, but near-term alpha is offshore.
sectors.ai: Buy the momentum: rotate into ETH and L2s (ARB, MNT) as the ETF narrative and staking flows accelerate; HYPE's +19% signals fresh speculative capital entering high-beta alts. Take profits on PEPE/ENA into strength, and add WLD on dips for AI-crypto crossover exposure. Indonesia's retail access remains thin, so use global venues; expect 10-15% pullback risk this week—trim into it, not out of it.
